skill.name: file-boundaries
skill.description: Defines file ownership boundaries for parallel implementation so agents know which files they may read, edit, create, or delete.
skill.summary: Coordinate parallel code work with clear file ownership and blocked-change rules.
skill.author: Clouder0

content.value_statement: Parallel implementation can cause agents to overwrite files from other workstreams. This skill defines ownership, read-only access, and blocked workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Defines owned files that agents may read, modify, create, or delete.
Defines read-only files that agents may inspect and import from.
Tells agents to stop when a needed change is outside ownership.
Provides a blocked-report format for boundary violations.
Explains how separate agents can work on different paths safely.
limitations: Does not enforce permissions in the operating system or repository.
Requires users to provide accurate ownership and read-only lists.
Does not resolve merge conflicts after boundaries are ignored.
Does not decide code architecture or task ownership by itself.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Feature Work
use_cases.description: Split feature implementation across agents while keeping each agent inside assigned files and directories.

use_cases.title: Protect Shared Type Files
use_cases.description: Allow agents to read shared types or utilities while blocking unapproved edits to those files.

use_cases.title: Report Blocked Changes Clearly
use_cases.description: Capture boundary violations with the needed file, reason, and suggested ownership update.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Ownership
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single file change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use file-boundaries. I own src/auth/login.ts and can read src/types/user.ts. Before editing, confirm the file is inside my ownership.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate two agents before implementation starts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use file-boundaries for two agents. Agent A owns src/auth. Agent B owns src/api. List allowed edits and blocked changes.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Read-Only Dependency
prompt_templates.scenario: Work near shared files without modifying them.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply file-boundaries while adding session logic. I own src/auth. I can read src/types/user.ts. Report blocked if type changes are required.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Boundary Compliance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before executing a multi-file plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this implementation plan with file-boundaries. Identify files outside ownership, read-only dependencies, and changes that should be blocked before work starts.

output_examples.input: A task needs to update authentication and reference shared user types.
output_examples.output: The agent edits only the authentication files, reads the shared types, and reports blocked if a type change is required.

output_examples.input: Two agents need to work on authentication and API routes at the same time.
output_examples.output: Each agent receives a separate ownership area, read-only dependencies, and a rule to stop before crossing boundaries.

output_examples.input: An implementation plan includes a change to an unowned utility file.
output_examples.output: The plan is marked blocked with the file name, reason for the requested change, and a suggested ownership update.

best_practices: List owned paths and read-only paths before implementation begins.
Keep ownership narrow enough to prevent unrelated edits.
Report blocked changes with the file, need, and suggested resolution.
anti_patterns: Editing read-only files because the change seems small.
Assuming ownership from nearby files or directory names.
Using broad ownership lists that hide real coordination problems.

faq.question: What does this skill help prevent?
faq.answer: It helps prevent agents from editing files that belong to another workstream.

faq.question: Does it enforce file permissions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides decision rules for agents and reviewers, not operating system enforcement.

faq.question: Can an agent read files it does not own?
faq.answer: Yes, when those files are listed as read-only boundaries for reference or imports.

faq.question: What happens when a needed edit is outside ownership?
faq.answer: The agent should stop and report the task as blocked with details.

faq.question: Is this useful for single-agent work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can still limit scope and reduce accidental changes.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
